land.text: Jinhan, whose rulers 'specifically claimed successorship over Jin state'

predecessors.note: Preceded by Jin (Korean state) on the Jinhan infobox.

land.text: Silla's first Cliopatria shape, identical to Jinhan's

successors.note: The infobox: 'Submission to Silla: 4th century CE'. Silla began as the statelet Saro inside the confederacy (Silla page).

keyframe_review.note: -91..372, 23,506 km2 (east of the Nakdong, 127.85-129.67E, 35.3-37.3N). The page places Jinhan on 'the southern peninsula, east of the Nakdong River valley' and lists twelve statelets from Andong and Sangju in the north to Ulsan, Miryang and Sacheon in the south; it gives no area. The shape holds Saro (Gyeongju) from the start, although the Silla page has Silla 'its own distinct political entity' by the 2nd century and 'the strongest constituent in the Jinhan confederacy' in the 3rd; the drawn Jinhan therefore overstates the confederacy from then, and the Silla dossier's start will decide how much. Unverified for those years: page budget.

373..377, the same outline and area. Cliopatria's Silla begins in 378 with exactly this shape (23,506 km2); the Silla page's 377 is the year Naemul's Silla 'sent emissaries to China and established relations with Goguryeo', not an annexation date.

region.text: 'a loose confederacy of chiefdoms ... on the southern peninsula, east of the Nakdong River valley'

ledger.note: 91 BCE: the Jinhan confederacy of twelve statelets appears in the south-east, led by Saro. Cliopatria's first year; the infobox says 'Establishment: 194 BCE' but the text 'from around the 1st century BCE', and the Samhan arose 'following the fall of Wiman Joseon in 108 BCE'.

377: Jinhan gives way to Silla. The Jinhan infobox says only 'Submission to Silla: 4th century CE'; the Silla page says Naemul (356-402) was king and that 'In 377, Silla sent emissaries to China and established relations with Goguryeo', the year Cliopatria ends Jinhan. The page gives no annexation year.

certainty.note: A confederacy of twelve statelets with no frontier on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a block of the south-east.

sources.title: Jinhan confederacy
sources.note: Identity, infobox (194 BCE, submission to Silla in the 4th century), the twelve statelets and their places, Saro 57 BCE, name Silla in 503, no area.

sources.title: Silla
sources.note: Silla as Saro inside Jinhan; distinct polity by the 2nd century; Naemul 356-402 and the 377 emissaries.

sources.title: Samhan
sources.note: Samhan formed around 108 BCE; Jinhan absorbed into Silla 'by the 4th century'.

notes: Cliopatria's Jinhan shape is carried unchanged to 377 and Silla's first shape (378) repeats it, so Cliopatria treats Jinhan and Silla as one handover; the Silla page has Saro founded 57 BCE (Samguk sagi, via the Jinhan page: 'founded by Bak Hyeokgeose in 57 BCE, who united the six clans of Jinhan'), a distinct polity by the 2nd century (Eumjipbeol, Siljikgok and Apdok taken in 102) and the strongest of the Jinhan in the 3rd; the Silla dossier (jk-02-c) should decide whether Silla starts before 378 and then trim this shape. The Jinhan page itself calls the records 'sparse and conflicting', gives 503 as the year Saro renamed itself Silla (the Silla page says 504), and calls the Qin-refugee origin 'mostly regarded as a false rumor'. Wei envoys visited Okjeo and Jinhan after the Goguryeo-Wei war (late 3rd century on the page), no territorial result. Capital: none; the confederacy had twelve statelets and Saro (Gyeongju) was the strongest, so no dot is drawn. The three Samhan infoboxes give 'Establishment: 194 BCE', contradicted by their texts; Cliopatria's -91 is kept (see korean-jin notes). Page budget: 3 pages of 2 (Silla and Samhan opened for the end and the start).
